title: session-fidelity-negotiator-prd-brainstorm
content:
Purpose / elevator
We need a lightweight runtime negotiation layer between client SDKs and Hosted API streaming sessions that lets clients declare and renegotiate session fidelity (e.g., full JSON typed output vs progressive text fragments), preferred tool-call semantics (sync vs async, hedging), and backpressure/latency tradeoffs. This doc sketches a pragmatic PRD: goals, API sketches, SDK ergonomics, rollout plan, and open questions.

Context / why now
- Customers building complex UIs want partial outputs streamed as typed frames while still supporting safe tool calls.
- Current hosted streaming surface streams tokens and ad-hoc JSON patches; SDKs handle heuristics in an inconsistent way.
- We are seeing customer workarounds: large client-side buffering, hand-rolled tool proxies, brittle resume logic.
- Opportunity: unify a small "negotiator" handshake to make fidelity explicit and reduce client-side complexity.

Problem statement
- Ambiguity: clients and the server implicitly assume different output guarantees (order, completeness, typed envelope).
- Tool invocation semantics are underspecified when responses are partial (e.g., tool call arrives mid-stream).
- Resuming interrupted streams is brittle: partial frames, duplicate tool calls, lost attachments.
- SDK ergonomics: developers copy/paste robust resume/backpressure logic across languages.

Goals (measurable)
- Reduce client-side resume-related bugs by 60% for customers adopting negotiator within 3 months.
- Reduce accidental duplicate tool invocations by 90% in canary rollout.
- Provide SDK primitives for 80% of common streaming patterns (progressive text, typed frames, tool calls, attachments).
- Keep added server latency < 2ms p99 for handshake layer.

Non-goals
- This is not a full protocol redesign. We assume existing streaming token APIs remain. Negotiator augments them.
- Not implementing complex multi-client session consensus; single-client session semantics only.

User stories
- As a mobile app developer, I want streamed progressive summaries (short text) by default and explicit typed action frames for tool calls so the UI can show incremental content and actionable buttons when available.
- As a platform engineer, I want a deterministic guarantee that a tool call will be executed at-most-once when the client opted into server-side idempotency.
- As an SDK author, I want a small set of primitives to implement resume+backpressure rather than bespoke code per customer.

Success metrics (tracking)
- Adoption rate: % of API sessions that send a negotiator payload in first 2 weeks after launch. Target 25% in canary cohort.
- Tool-call duplicates: number of duplicate-tool-execution incidents per 10k toolcalls. Target < 1.
- Resume errors: percentage of resume attempts that report frame-mismatch errors. Target < 2%.
- Developer feedback: qualitative NPS from 10 pilot customers.

Constraints and considerations
- Backwards compatibility: existing clients must continue functioning if they ignore negotiator.
- Minimal surface area: handshake must be compact (small JSON) and optional.
- Security: any new metadata must flow through current access controls and audit logs; tool-call idempotency metadata must not leak sensitive ids in logs.

Design sketch: high level
- Client sends an optional JSON negotiator in the initial streaming request (HTTP header or first control frame). Negotiator fields: fidelity_profile, tool_semantics, resume_mode, telemetry_level.
- Server replies with accepted_profile and server_constraints immediately in a single control frame (0ms extra for majority of cases).
- During stream, typed frames are emitted as compact framed envelopes: each envelope has frame_id, frame_type, seq, partial (bool), checksum, payload. Frames may be text fragments, structured JSON action, or attachment references.
- Tool calls are surfaced as frame_type = "tool_request" with a tool_call_id and idempotency_hint. Server will only execute tool if handshake accepted tool_semantics that allow server-executed tool calls.
- Resume protocol: client asks for session delta from last-seen frame_id; server responds with non-overlapping frames plus a resume_token. Resume_token encodes low-entropy proof of last-committed server state, rotated per session.

Negotiator schema (first-pass)
- fidelity_profile: string ("text-first", "typed-actions", "strict-typed-json")
- prefer_partial_frames: boolean
- tool_semantics: string ("client-only", "server-execute-idempotent", "server-execute-hedged")
- resume_mode: string ("none", "delta", "checkpoint")
- telemetry_level: string ("minimal", "standard", "verbose")
- max_frame_size_bytes: integer (hint)

Server response schema
- accepted_profile: string
- server_constraints: array of short strings
- session_id: string (opaque)
- resume_token: string (opaque)

Frame envelope example (pseudo)
- {frame_id: "f_000123", type: "action", seq: 7, partial: true, payload: "{\"action\":\"suggest_edit\"}", checksum: "sha1:..."}

Tool-call flow variants
- client-only: client calls tool locally after parsing a tool_request frame; server will not execute.
- server-execute-idempotent: server will execute tool once and return tool_response frame; includes idempotency_hint for safe retry.
- server-execute-hedged: server may call multiple model variants or fallback tools; client opts-in for lower-latency but eventually consistent semantics.

SDK ergonomics (priority list)
- Provide a small language-agnostic set of primitives in SDKs: negotiate(sessionOptions), onFrame(handler), requestResume(lastFrameId), toolCallGuard(toolCallId) -> promise.
- High-level helpers: progressiveText(handler), typedAction(handler), safeToolInvoke(toolSpec, opts) that implement idempotency and retries for the user.
- Local dev ergonomics: debug flag to log control frames and frame checksums; simulate truncated frames and resume paths.
- Mobile-specific surface: prefer_partial_frames default true, resume_mode default = checkpoint for unstable networks.

Backpressure and latency pathways
- Negotiator includes prefer_partial_frames and max_frame_size_bytes to indicate client-side memory constraints.
- Server may emit frames at a reduced fidelity if client signals tight latency SLO. Server_constraints will include a degrade_to value (e.g., "text-first") if needed.
- SDK exposes a per-session token bucket that maps to server_constraints for client-side drop/merge behavior.

Migration / rollout plan
- Week 0: internal alpha behind feature flag. SDK prototypes in JS and Kotlin. Canary customers invited.
- Week 2: collect telemetry, iterate schema (remove noisy fields).
- Week 6: expand canary to 10 customers; integrate server-side idempotency store for tool calls.
- Week 10: default negotiator available; backward-compatible fallback remains.

Observability / telemetry
- Control-frame counts, negotiation success rate, handshake latency p50/p95/p99.
- Tool-call execution vs refusal rates. Duplicate tool execution detections.
- Resume success ratio and average time to resume.
- SDK-level telemetry: frames dropped, partial->final upgrade counts.

Security and privacy notes
- Resume_token must be opaque and cryptographically-hardened to prevent forging or replay.
- Tool idempotency_hint must avoid embedding PII. Use hashed identifiers.
- Audit events: negotiated profile, tool-call acceptance, resume requests logged with session_id and owner only.

Open questions / risks
- How to guarantee at-most-once for server-executed tools at scale without high-latency persistent store? (we may accept eventual idempotency store with TTL)
- Should negotiator be an HTTP header or first control frame? Header is simpler for proxies; control frame is more expressive.
- Risk: clients may over-opt into aggressive server-execute-hedged mode causing unexpected side effects. Need safety rate limits.
- Interoperability: how to make this map cleanly onto existing incremental JSON patching experiments?

Next steps / immediate action items
- Prototype negotiator control-frame encoding in the JS streaming lib. (owner: Julian Kim)
- Add basic SDK primitives to rw-js and rw-kotlin with feature flag. (owner: Riley Stone)
- Spike: simple idempotency store for tool calls with 24h TTL; measure latency p95. (owner: María González)
- Draft API docs and quickstart sample showing progressive text -> typed action button sequence. (owner: Asha Patel)

Notes to self / loose thoughts
- Keep negotiator tiny. Start conservative: fidelity_profile selection + tool_semantics + resume_mode. Add telemetry later.
- Consider a "shadow-apply" run where server simulates server-execute but doesn't actually call tool; logs discrepancy to help customers migrate.
- UX: for mobile offline flows, checkpoint resume + attachments will be the killer feature.
- Add a small conformance test harness to the streaming simulator that can fuzz partial frames and resume sequences.

Attachments: sketches, quickflow diagrams, and a mock transcript will be attached after first proto.
